expect.text: Luck, whatever the choices: a crash runs from age 29 to 32, and {firstName} loses the job at 32, in the last year of it. With the reference plan, no year needs borrowing.
The job ends at 32, in the last year of the crash. With the reference plan the savings and cash cover it without any borrowing.
With the reference plan the money lasts, with about ₹13 crore spendable at 60 in today's rupees. {firstName} lives only to 68 on this luck, so retirement is short; how long a life lasts is luck too.
Going for growth beats the reference plan on this luck: about ₹19 crore spendable at 60, against about ₹13 crore. It also swings more in the crash years.

The same growth plan on seed 36 ends with only about ₹2 crore spendable at 60, ten times less, and below what the reference plan would have made on that seed (about ₹2.9 crore). Same plan, different luck: a late run of crashes from 48 to 54 hit just before retirement.

provenance.basis: Checked by replaying seeds 35 and 36 with the picks above (tests: scripts.test.js). Figures are in today's rupees and are illustrative, like the rest of the game; if the model is retuned the test says which lines to revisit.
